content: Nafcillin is a medication typically administered by a healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. It is important to inform your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions and any prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using. This helps determine if nafcillin is appropriate for you. If you are allergic to penicillin, other medications, corn, or corn products, you should not use nafcillin. Additionally, individuals with asthma, liver disease, kidney disease, or a history of antibiotic-associated diarrhea should discuss these conditions with their healthcare provider before starting nafcillin. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider, as it is not known how nafcillin may affect pregnancy or an unborn baby. Similarly, if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, let your provider know, as nafcillin can pass into breast milk. Nafcillin may interact with other medications, such as tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline, minocycline), warfarin (a blood thinner), cyclosporine (an immune suppressant), and probenecid (used for gout). Always discuss any medications or supplements you are taking with your healthcare provider to avoid potential interactions. If you miss a dose of nafcillin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the full prescribed course of nafcillin, even if your symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of developing antibiotic resistance. In the event of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Overdosing on nafcillin may require discontinuation of the medication, and a healthcare provider may provide treatment and supportive care as needed. Common side effects of nafcillin include pain, swelling, or inflammation at the injection site, as well as rashes. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, though less common, include severe allergic reactions (e.g., difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, hives, or dizziness), seizures, kidney damage (e.g., reduced urination, swelling in the legs, or chest pain), liver damage (e.g., jaundice, dark urine, or abdominal pain), and antibiotic-associated diarrhea caused by Clostridioides difficile (e.g., watery or bloody diarrhea, severe stomach cramps). If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Nafcillin does not have known interactions with food or drinks, but heavy alcohol consumption may weaken your immune response and make it harder for your body to fight infections. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and up-to-date information regarding nafcillin and its use.
